caption: The drawing consists of a central object resembling a stylized plant or flower with a turquoise cylindrical stem and yellow, fan-shaped leaves or petals with red and black curling tendrils at the top of the stem. This object is positioned in the center of the composition. Surrounding the central object are several nested rectangular frames: the innermost has a wavy-edge pink border, followed by a thicker pinkish-red frame, then a thinner dark brown frame, and an outermost rectangular frame with light green and blue sections on the corners and top, as well as pinkish-red sections on the sides. The background within the innermost frame is a light pink, while the other frames have alternating shades of pink, green, and blue. The overall composition is symmetrical, with the central object and frames aligned with the center of a cream-colored background. In the lower left corner, the number "26" is written in small blue text.
title: Plate 16: Altar Panel: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
